attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
High fever and irritability for the past two days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
A 4-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents due to a high fever and irritability for the past two days.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- X-linked Chronic Granulomatous Disease
- History of recurrent pneumonia (3 episodes)
- Recurrent cutaneous abscesses

The child has a history of multiple skin and lung infections since infancy, including a previous hospitalization for pneumonia. His mother reports that his infections are often difficult to treat and require prolonged courses of antibiotics.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Incision and drainage of subcutaneous abscess, left thigh (age 2 years)
- Bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tube placement (age 3 years)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 80mg/400mg (1 teaspoon) oral once daily
- Itraconazole 100mg oral solution once daily
- Interferon-gamma-1b 50 mcg/m2 subcutaneous injection 3 times weekly

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 6 from severe recurrent infections (presumed undiagnosed X-linked CGD)
- Mother: asymptomatic carrier of X-linked Chronic Granulomatous Disease
- Father: healthy
- No siblings

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 39.2°C (102.5°F), heart rate is 120/min, and respiratory rate is 24/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears ill and has several swollen, tender lymph nodes in the cervical region.

LABORATORY DATA:
A complete blood count shows leukocytosis with a predominance of neutrophils.

IMAGING:
A chest X-ray reveals a lobar consolidation in the right lower lobe.

OTHER STUDIES:
Blood cultures are drawn

PLAN:
Empirical intravenous antibiotics are initiated

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. James Okafor, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever, cough, and difficulty breathing for three days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 4-year-old male with X-linked Chronic Granulomatous Disease and recurrent pneumonia returns for outpatient evaluation, brought by his mother due to a 3-day history of fever, cough, and difficulty breathing.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chronic granulomatous disease (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- X-linked Chronic Granulomatous Disease
- History of recurrent pneumonia (3 episodes)
- Recurrent cutaneous abscesses

His immunizations are up to date.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Incision and drainage of subcutaneous abscess, left thigh (age 2 years)
- Bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tube placement (age 3 years)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 80mg/400mg (1 teaspoon) oral once daily
- Itraconazole 100mg oral solution once daily
- Interferon-gamma-1b 50 mcg/m2 subcutaneous injection 3 times weekly

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 6 from severe recurrent infections (presumed undiagnosed X-linked CGD)
- Mother: asymptomatic carrier of X-linked Chronic Granulomatous Disease
- Father: healthy
- No siblings

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
The child's temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate is 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 40 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears lethargic and is breathing rapidly. Auscultation of the chest reveals decreased breath sounds in the right upper lobe.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory values:
- White blood cell count: 15,000/mm³
- Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL
- Platelet count: 250,000/mm³
- C-reactive protein: 40 mg/L (normal <10 mg/L)

IMAGING:
The pediatrician orders a frontal chest x-ray, which shows an opacity in the right upper lobe without evidence of a large thymic silhouette.
